instruction: Texture-Link Repair `/home/user/Desktop/scene.blend` contains three mesh planes `Plane_R`, `Plane_G`, `Plane_B` at x=-2, 0, +2. Each plane has a material with an Image Texture node whose image datablock has a BROKEN `filepath` (pointing at a path that does not exist on disk). The correct 16x16 solid-colour PNGs are on disk at `/home/user/Desktop/textures/red.png`, `/home/user/Desktop/textures/green.png`, and `/home/user/Desktop/textures/blue.png`. The image datablocks are named `red_diffuse`, `green_diffuse`, `blue_diffuse` (one per plane). Your task is to re-point each broken image's filepath to the correct PNG in `/home/user/Desktop/textures/` and save the result to `/home/user/Desktop/answer.blend` (relative to the working directory). ## What to do 1. Use the initial scene at `/home/user/Desktop/scene.blend`. 2. Ensure the three PNGs are reachable from the location of the new blend. The simplest way is to copy `/home/user/Desktop/textures/*.png` into the Desktop root so Blender-relative `//<color>.png` paths resolve next to `/home/user/Desktop/answer.blend`. 3. Save-as `/home/user/Desktop/answer.blend` first (so `//` anchors at the Desktop directory). 4. For each broken image datablock, use the image name (contains `red`, `green`, or `blue`) to determine which colour it wants, then set `image.filepath = '//<color>.png'` (and `image.filepath_raw` to the same value), call `image.reload()` to re-bind, and optionally `image.pack()` so the pixels survive save-close-reopen. 5. Save the blend. ## Requirements 1. `/home/user/Desktop/answer.blend` exists and opens as a valid Blender file. 2. The three planes `Plane_R`, `Plane_G`, `Plane_B` all still exist as mesh objects, each with a material whose node tree contains an Image Texture node with an assigned image. 3. Every disk-backed image datablock (excluding `Render Result` / `Viewer Node`) resolves to a real file on disk (or is packed) AND loads successfully after reopen - i.e. no image is missing. 4. Rendering the scene (Eevee, 256x256) succeeds. 5. In the rendered image, the ROI at each plane's projected world centre shows the correct dominant colour channel: Plane_R shows red, Plane_G shows green, Plane_B shows blue. This proves both the path repair AND that the correct texture was assigned to each plane. Do not rename objects, materials, or image datablocks; do not alter the shader graphs; only the image filepaths (and the texture files' location on disk) should change. [Software] Launch Blender by running `blender` from a terminal.
